title: Shortness of breath and non-productive cough - Internal Medicine

stacks.label: Ordered: Pulse oximetry
stacks.finding: Patient has HIV and is coughing. It's important to check for oxygenation.

stacks.label: Ordered: Arterial Blood Gases
stacks.finding: Important piece in this hypoxemic patient.

stacks.label: Ordered: Electrocardiography, 12 lead / Electrocardiography, ambulatory / Electrocardiography, rhythm strip, long
stacks.finding: An EKG should be done to rule out any cardiac causes of the patient's presentation.

stacks.label: Ordered: Microscopic examination, vaginal fluid / Cervical wet mount
stacks.finding: The patient has a yeast infection due to poorly controlled HIV. Microscopy of the discharge with 10% KOH will often reveal hyphae or budding yeast in 50%-70% of cases.

stacks.label: Ordered: Hepatitis panel
stacks.finding: A patient with symptomatic HIV should be screened for other common co-occurring diseases.

stacks.label: Ordered: Bacterial culture, blood
stacks.finding: Considering this patient is high risk for infection due to her immunocompromised status, a blood culture would be warranted in this case.

stacks.label: Ordered: Gram stain, sputum
stacks.finding: It's important to rule out bacterial infection.

stacks.label: Ordered: Mycobacterial culture, sputum / Acid fast stain, sputum
stacks.finding: Tuberculosis is often seen in immunocompromised patients. It is important to check whether patient's symptoms may be due to tuberculosis.

stacks.label: Ordered: Bacterial culture, sputum
stacks.finding: It's important to rule out bacterial infection.

hpi_narrative: A 30-year-old male with known HIV positivity presents with shortness of breath and non-productive cough. He is experiencing fever and fatigue.
